stories.title: The truth about the viral 9/11 petition targeting Mamdani
stories.text: On Sunday, the New York Post, the Rupert Murdoch-owned tabloid, ran a story on its cover under this blaring headline: “STAY AWAY: Thousands of 9/11 families demand Mamdani be banned from 25th-Anniversary.” The New York Post story is about a petition on Change.org started by Giovanni Galante, whose wife Grace Catherine Galante was among the nearly 3,000 victims of the 9/11 attacks. “[W]e, the family members of those murdered on 9/11, write to express our concern regarding the potential inclusion of Zohran Mamdani in the 25th-year commemorative events,” the petition states. The story went viral on right-wing social media, garnering millions of views on X. Within hours, the story was being featured on Fox News, the cable network that is also owned by Murdoch. “I can fully understand why the families wouldn’t want him there,” Fox News pundit Tomi Lahren said Sunday. On the same program, Fox News’ Senior National Correspondent Rich Edson suggested that Mamdani could demonstrate “respect” for the families by not showing up. stories.title: Israeli Settlers Set Up At Least Six New Colonial Outposts After Friday Killings in the Occupied West Bank
stories.text: RAMALLAH, occupied West Bank—In the aftermath of Friday’s killings in the village of Tal, hundreds of armed Israeli settlers and soldiers launched a campaign of terror targeting Palestinian towns and villages across the occupied West Bank, with reports of home raids, shootings, assaults, mass detentions, and demolitions of property—including residential buildings, mosques, cars, agricultural equipment, and farmland. It began when armed settlers raided Tal, which is southwest of Nablus city in the northern West Bank, at around 7 a.m. local time and opened fire. They were confronted by Palestinian residents of the village who were attempting to protect their homes and land. Just a week earlier, armed settlers had raided Tal and set fire to a Palestinian home. The family managed to escape before the house was consumed by flames. During Friday’s attack, one of the Palestinian residents, Farouq Ramadan, a father of five, managed to seize the machine gun of an Israeli settler in a moment captured on camera. stories.title: Drone Strikes Are Destroying the Infrastructure of Survival in the Heart of Sudan
stories.text: Story by Mohamed Wad Al-Sak Ahmed Mahmoud’s sister, Nafisah, died last month in the city of El-Obeid, another victim of a more than three-year long war raging across Sudan already considered one of the deadliest conflicts for civilians this century. But like a growing number of Sudanese victims of the war, Mahmoud’s sister’s death was not the direct result of an airstrike, or gunfire. Instead, she fell victim to the near-total collapse of basic infrastructure in the country as a result of calculated attacks aimed at depriving Sudanese civilians the necessities of life. The war in Sudan has now killed somewhere between 150,000 to 400,000 people according to outside analysts, with people dying from a combination of direct violence, hunger, and lack of access to healthcare. In June, the 21-year-old Nafisah suddenly fell faint and needed urgent hospital care; she had been managing the impact of an under-treated blood clot in her left leg since 2024. stories.title: “Get Lit” Livestream, 4:30 pm ET: The Comic Climax of Dostoyevsky's "Demons"
stories.text: “And I proclaim,” Stepan Trofimovich shrieked, in the last extremity of passion, “and I proclaim that Shakespeare and Raphael are higher than the emancipation of the serfs, higher than nationality, higher than socialism, higher than the younger generation… ” With this outburst at a provincial fête, Stepan Verkhovensky — one of the main characters of Fyodor Dostoyevsky’s Demons — seals his fate as the enemy of political progress, in the eyes of a movement he’s loved all his life. It’s one of a list of comic twists in a critical portion of the novel, which Brad Pearce and I will be back discussing today. stories.title: History's Most Preventable Terror Attack?
stories.text: On Saturday evening, a German-born man attacked a Pride Parade, first chasing people with a machete, then driving a van into a crowd, and finally running “toward officers with a sharp instrument” before being shot dead in the town of Spandau. One woman was killed, and 29 other were injured at the Christopher Street Day event, which was guarded by 2,200 police officers, up from 1,300 last year. “How did he even get into the Tiergarten?” one attendee was quoted as saying. “There were anti-car and anti-truck barriers everywhere.” Berlin-born Abdel Ballout got past more than anti-car and anti-truck barriers to make his attack.
